summary: With no memory limit, Table::raw_set and create_table_from call lua_rawset unprotected, so a nil or NaN key raises a Lua error with no handler and aborts the process instead of returning Err.
Table == slice ignores extra slice elements, so a table equals any longer slice with the same prefix, and an empty table equals every slice.
HashSet and BTreeSet of integers do not round trip, because into_lua makes {[1]=true,...} but from_lua sees a positive raw length and reads the true values as elements.
Value equality casts Integer to f64, so large integers compare equal to floats with a different mathematical value.
